claims.says: ~10,500 ft cumulative gain

contradictions.why: The header/TECHNICAL STATS gain_ft (5,980 ft) is roughly half the cumulative gain the route's own 6-day itinerary adds up to (10,500 ft) and states explicitly in its own totalNote.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The itinerary's per-day gainFt figures and its totalNote agree with each other at ~10,500 ft; gain_ft is the outlier.

claims.says: elev 6903

claims.field: bivy[0] ("Cache Col and the Cache Glacier shoulder")
claims.says: elev 6400 (implied, camp is described at/below the col)

contradictions.why: The same named col is effectively given two elevations roughly 500 ft apart, more than double the usual ~250 ft tolerance.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The bivy entry itself hedges ('treat the elevation as approximate, since published figures for the col vary by a couple of hundred feet'), suggesting the surveyed waypoint figure (6,903 ft) is likelier correct, but the row does not resolve it definitively.

contradictions.fact: Trip structure / which outing this route's fields describe

claims.says: the accepted approach follows the southern leg of the Ptarmigan Traverse corridor out of the Downey Creek Trailhead ... almost everyone treats this as a 2-3 day round trip ... matching the ~29-mile (46.67 km) round-trip distance
Downey Creek Trailhead (Trail #768, Suiattle River Road)

Parties who are instead walking the full Ptarmigan Traverse pick Lizard up mid-route and carry on to the other end, finishing at Cascade Pass rather than Downey Creek -- that is a shuttle trip and a different outing from the approach described here.
Cascade Pass to Kool-Aid Lake
A 6-day, ~34 mi one-way traverse (shuttle required) with ~10,500 ft cumulative gain

contradictions.why: The route's own approach/descent text frames this route as an out-and-back from the Downey Creek Trailhead and explicitly calls the Cascade-Pass-to-Downey-Creek shuttle traverse 'a different outing' -- yet the itinerary actually attached to this route IS that one-way, two-trailhead shuttle traverse (day 1 starts at Cascade Pass; day 6 ends at Downey Creek Trailhead), contradicting the single-trailhead framing used everywhere else on the row.

contradictions.fact: Waypoint distance chain splices two unconnected trailheads

claims.says: distMi 0
distMi 3.7

contradictions.why: The waypoints list runs Downey Creek Trailhead (distMi 0) directly into Cascade Pass (distMi 3.7) as if contiguous, but Cascade Pass is reached from a separate, distant northern trailhead on Cascade River Road, not from Downey Creek; the southern approach (Bachelor Creek, Cub Lake, Itswoot Ridge) that the row calls its primary/accepted route is entirely absent from the waypoints list.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The rest of the waypoint chain (Cache Col onward) is internally consistent as distances from Cascade Pass; the Downey Creek Trailhead entry at distMi 0 appears spliced in from a different route.

contradictions.fact: Whether the Downey Creek/Suiattle exit is usable as a bail route

claims.says: Do not count on reaching the Downey Creek/Suiattle River Road exit, which is currently closed by flood damage.
the Downey Creek trailhead itself remains reachable on foot or by bike beyond the closure, adding several miles each way

contradictions.why: bail implies the exit route is unusable, while road.closures and pro_tips say it remains reachable on foot/bike, just longer.
contradictions.internal_resolution: road.closures/pro_tips give the fuller picture (still reachable, just longer); bail's blanket 'do not count on reaching it' overstates the closure.

claims.says: Jul-Sep; snow lingers in the summit gully into June in most years
Late June through September ... Trip reports document successful climbs from late May onward
Approach gullies and upper slopes typically still snow-covered ... outside the recommended scramble window; status: risky

contradictions.why: best_season recommends starting in late June (and even notes successful climbs from late May), which falls before the season field's stated July start and is explicitly rated 'risky'/outside the recommended window by the route's own seasonal_guidance.
contradictions.internal_resolution: season and seasonal_guidance.monthBreakdown agree the window doesn't really open until July; best_season is the outlier.

claims.says: 4 numbered rows: '1. Foggy Lake to shoulder', '2. Shoulder to notch', '3. Notch to sub-notch', '4. Sub-notch to summit'

contradictions.why: The route's own pitch-count field says 2 pitches, but the ROUTE BREAKDOWN (pitch_detail) lists four separately numbered stages for the same line.
contradictions.internal_resolution: pitch_detail is the more granular, itemized source and should govern; pitches=2 looks stale.

claims.says: Foggy Lake (~5,200 ft, 3.3 miles from the trailhead)
up boulder and talus slopes to Foggy Lake at about 5,200 ft, roughly 3.3 miles in
distMi 4.8

contradictions.why: Two prose fields agree Foggy Lake is 3.3 miles from the trailhead, but the waypoint entry for the same lake gives distMi 4.8 -- a 1.5-mile (~45%) discrepancy for the route's main staging/water point.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Both narrative fields (approach, approach_variants) agree at 3.3 mi; the waypoint's 4.8 is the outlier.

claims.says: Begin descent 10:45 AM ... Back at trailhead 2:30 PM

contradictions.why: The stated descentTimeHrs (2.5 hr) doesn't match the ~3h45m the route's own clock-time schedule shows between beginning the descent (10:45 AM) and reaching the trailhead (2:30 PM).
contradictions.internal_resolution: The itemized schedule has specific clock times and is more granular; descentTimeHrs appears understated relative to it.

contradictions.fact: Hardest grade on the route (Class 3 vs Class 4)

claims.says: Class 3 + snow/glacier
Class 3-4
grade Class 3-4
a short, exposed 4th-class knife-edge section
some parties rate it Class 3, others Class 4 depending on line and conditions

contradictions.why: The top-level grade field caps the route at Class 3, but rock_grade, the summit-block pitch, and the descent text all describe Class 4 moves on the chossy summit block/knife-edge.
contradictions.internal_resolution: rock_grade, pitch_detail, beta and descent_text agree the route reaches Class 4; grade undercounts it.

claims.says: Total elevation gain from trailhead to the 7,282-ft high point is roughly 5,200 ft

contradictions.why: gain_ft (6,023) is about 800 ft (~14%) higher than both the itinerary's gainFt and the approach text's own explicit '~5,200 ft' statement.
contradictions.internal_resolution: itinerary and approach text agree at ~5,200 ft; gain_ft is the outlier.

claims.says: roughly 5,200 ft over about 9-9.5 miles one-way, consistent with a ~19 km round-trip figure
~12 miles round trip
distMi 7.3

contradictions.why: The approach text's own '9-9.5 miles one-way' claim is internally inconsistent with the '~19 km round-trip' figure in that same sentence (9-9.5 mi one-way implies ~18-19 mi / ~29-30 km round trip, not 19 km/12 mi), and it also disagrees with the itinerary/totalNote's ~12-mile round trip, dist_km (11.1 km = ~6.9 mi), and the waypoints' own cumulative one-way distance to the summit (7.3 mi).
contradictions.internal_resolution: itinerary, totalNote, dist_km and the waypoint chain all cluster around a ~7-mile one-way / ~12-mile round-trip distance; the approach text's '9-9.5 miles one-way' figure is the outlier and self-contradicts its own round-trip claim.

claims.says: 30m rope for the roped chimney section (three moves: 5.6, 5.2, 5.6)
a 60m rope
A single 60m rope is sufficient to reach easier ground
1 rappel off the bolted anchor above the crux chimney; 60m rope reported sufficient

contradictions.why: rope_length_m and rack both specify a 30 m rope, but detailed_rack, descent_text and the rappels field all say a 60 m rope is what's needed for the rappel -- a party equipped per rope_length_m/rack would carry half the rope length the row itself says the descent requires.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Three fields (detailed_rack, descent_text, rappels) agree on 60 m; rope_length_m and rack are the outliers.

moat/crevasse hazard at col
